stories.headline: OpenAI told investors its run rate is near $50B, not ~$70B; AI stocks slide

key_facts.fact: On October 8 the Financial Times reported that OpenAI told prospective investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion, well below the $68 billion figure widely reported in September.
key_facts.excerpt: A report today by the Financial Times revealed that OpenAI recently told prospective investors that its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion – far below the $68 billion figure that was widely reported two months ago.

key_facts.fact: According to a person familiar with the matter cited by CNBC, the $68 billion figure included gross revenue from OpenAI's partners to allow comparison with Anthropic, while the new figure is net revenue; the gap does not reflect lost sales.
key_facts.excerpt: The discrepancy between the two revenue figures does not reflect a loss of sales. CNBC cited a person familiar with the matter who explained that the $68 billion number incorporated gross revenue from partner companies, a methodology investors used to put OpenAI's performance on equal footing with Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI also told investors its total run rate grew 77% in the third quarter and its enterprise run rate grew 107%.
key_facts.excerpt: In addition to the $50 billion figure, OpenAI also pointed to 77% growth in its annual revenue run rate during the third quarter, as well as a 107% growth in run rate for its enterprise business.

key_facts.fact: Oracle fell about 5.5%, CoreWeave about 8% and Nvidia 2.9% on October 8; the Nasdaq dropped 1.25%, its worst day since mid-August.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nasdaq index fell 1.25% today, its worst single-day performance since mid-August... Oracle Corp... falling 5.5%... Nvidia Corp. declined 2.9%. CoreWeave Inc.... suffered an 8% drop

key_facts.fact: At $50 billion, OpenAI's $852 billion March valuation equals about 17 times run-rate revenue rather than 12.5 times; OpenAI is in early talks on a new round of around $30 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: It leaves OpenAI's $852 billion March valuation at 17 times run-rate revenue, not 12.5... The $1.4 trillion target comes from Bloomberg's report on the roughly $30 billion round now in early talks

key_facts.fact: OpenAI posted a net loss of $38.5 billion in 2025 on $13.07 billion in revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI posted a net loss of $38.5 billion in 2025 on $13.07 billion in revenue.

stories.headline: OpenAI says fired safety researchers breached trust, denies retaliation for safety concerns

key_facts.fact: In a note from its research leaders posted on X on October 9, OpenAI said it parted ways with Jasmine Wang, Mikita Balesni and Tomek Korbak after an investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said its investigation uncovered 'a significant breach of trust beyond what's outlined in the letter they published' but did not specify the conduct.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what's outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it is finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks, and agreed that preserving monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment.
key_facts.excerpt: We are actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks... We agree with the letter that preserving the monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment, including from OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Korbak said he was told he was fired over how he communicated with METR, the independent evaluator OpenAI brought in to investigate the Hugging Face sandbox-escape incident; he said talking to METR was his job.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr Korbak said in a post on X that he was told he was being sacked because of the way he communicated with METR, an independent non-profit AI evaluation firm that OpenAI brought in to investigate the Hugging Face incident.

key_facts.fact: Balesni wrote that he believes the three were 'fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation.'
key_facts.excerpt: He wrote on X that he believes the three were "fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation".

key_facts.fact: The researchers said in their letter they were not the source of a September article in The Information about security concerns around OpenAI's Astra model.
key_facts.excerpt: Wang, Korbak and Balesni said in their letter they were not the source of a news article published on The Information last month about security concerns around OpenAI's latest AI model "Astra".

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission: free AI vulnerability scans for open source, grid defense program

key_facts.fact: Anthropic on October 8 launched the Anthropic Cyber Mission, starting with critical infrastructure and open-source software.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on... We're starting with two areas

key_facts.fact: The Critical Infrastructure Defense Program brings frontier Claude models, on-site engineers and threat research to 11 founding partners: Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC and Rockwell Automation.
key_facts.excerpt: Its founding partners are Accenture, Booz Allen, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Dragos, Hitachi, Insane Cyber, Nozomi Networks, Palo Alto Networks, PwC, and Rockwell Automation.

key_facts.fact: OSS Scanner, inspired by Google's OSS-Fuzz, gives opted-in open-source projects free periodic scans from Anthropic's strongest models, including Claude Mythos, with reports sent without human review.
key_facts.excerpt: The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage... These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos)

key_facts.fact: Anthropic expects a true-positive rate above 90%; expert penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings from an early version across 48 projects and cleared 85 for disclosure.
key_facts.excerpt: The expert penetration testers who vet the company's coordinated disclosures checked 97 critical and high-severity findings from an early version across 48 projects and cleared 85 for disclosure.

key_facts.fact: By October 2026 Anthropic had reviewed over 6,000 vulnerability reports through its human-reviewed coordinated disclosure process.
key_facts.excerpt: By October 2026, we had reviewed over 6,000 such reports.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic noted that operational technology systems often cannot be taken offline for patching, so known vulnerabilities can remain unresolved for years.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic noted that OT systems often cannot be taken offline for patching, so known vulnerabilities can remain unresolved for years.

stories.headline: Anthropic's usage policy update bans 'sustained and needless' abuse of Claude, election deception

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published its 2026 usage policy update on October 8, its first in over a year, adding a prohibition on 'sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior' toward its models.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is making changes to its usage policy for the first time in over a year... one of the most significant changes prohibits "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward Claude.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said the rule applies only in extreme cases with no discernible purpose, not to ordinary frustration, dark creative themes or model testing, and that Claude ending conversations remains the primary enforcement mechanism.
key_facts.excerpt: It does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research... Claude's ability to end these interactions will remain the primary enforcement mechanism.

key_facts.fact: The update also codifies prohibitions on election interference, weapons development and surveillance, and adds controls for when Claude autonomously takes physical actions.
key_facts.excerpt: It draws on new patterns of misuse in influence operations, weapons development, and surveillance... to add controls for when Claude is used to autonomously take physical actions, and to address abusive behavior toward our models.

key_facts.fact: The updated usage policy takes effect on November 12, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The updated usage policy takes effect on November 12.

key_facts.fact: The policy forbids using Claude to 'deceive voters or disrupt elections' as US midterm elections approach.
key_facts.excerpt: clarifying that, as US midterm elections loom, it cannot be used to "deceive voters or disrupt elections".

stories.headline: OpenAI bans Russian and Iranian influence ops that planted ChatGPT-aided stories in real outlets

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on October 8 it banned ChatGPT account clusters tied to Russian and Iranian covert influence operations that ran 'false front' entities.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Thursday (Oct 8) said it banned clusters of accounts traced to Russia and Iran, for using its ChatGPT AI assistant to support covert influence operations.

key_facts.fact: The Russian operation ran a fake think tank, the Social Research Center, staffed by unwitting employees in Latin America; OpenAI called it the most complex front-identity attempt it had disrupted in two and a half years.
key_facts.excerpt: The Russian operation co-opted "unwitting people" in Latin America to run a "think-tank" -- called the Social Research Center (SRC)... "This stands out as the most complex attempt to run a front identity that we've disrupted over the past two and a half years."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI rated the Russian campaign Category 5 of 6 on the influence-operations impact scale, the first Category 5 it has disrupted, citing evidence it prompted public comment by politicians.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI rated the Russian campaign a five — the second-highest level... This was the first Category 5 operation OpenAI had disrupted since it began publishing such reports

key_facts.fact: The Iranian operation, 'Bogus Bylines,' used seven fake Western journalist personas to place nearly 100 articles about the US-Iran conflict in about a dozen outlets between July 2025 and October 2026; OpenAI rated it Category 4.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI identified nearly 100 articles that were published or syndicated to about a dozen outlets between July 2025 and October 2026. These were written under seven fictitious bylines

key_facts.fact: Outlets that published the fake-byline articles included Daily Kos and the UK-based Middle East Monitor, which ran at least 21 articles by four fake authors, according to NBC News.
key_facts.excerpt: The fake authors published articles in outlets including the progressive U.S. news site Daily Kos and the U.K.-based Middle East Monitor. According to NBC News, the Middle East Monitor published at least 21 articles by four fake authors.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the Iranian activity appeared consistent with a commercial actor running a for-hire influence campaign but did not identify it.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said the operation's activity "appeared consistent with a commercial actor running a for-hire influence campaign" but that it was unable to identify who that was.

stories.headline: OpenAI rolls out Ultrafast GPT-6.1 Sol, up to 8x faster at six times the API price

key_facts.fact: OpenAI on October 8 began rolling out Ultrafast for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work, promising near-Astra intelligence at up to 8x the speed of Sol Standard.
key_facts.excerpt: Ultrafast is rolling out today for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work. Near-Astra intelligence at up to 8x fa…

key_facts.fact: Ultrafast API pricing is six times Standard: $12 per million input tokens, $0.60 cached input and $60 per million output tokens at short context, versus Standard rates of $2 and $10.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast costs $12 per million input tokens, $0.60 for cached input, $15 for cache writes and $60 for output at short context. That is exactly six times the Standard rates of $2, $0.10, $2.50 and $10.

key_facts.fact: In Codex and ChatGPT Work, Ultrafast is limited to the Pro $500 plan and eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces, and counts against subscription limits at 8x the Standard rate.
key_facts.excerpt: In Codex and ChatGPT Work, Ultrafast is limited to Pro $500 and eligible Enterprise and Edu plans... Ultrafast counts against included subscription limits at 8x the Standard rate

key_facts.fact: AWS made GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast available on Amazon Bedrock the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, AWS announces the availability of Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol from OpenAI on Amazon Bedrock.

key_facts.fact: Epoch AI noted OpenAI halved GPT-6.1 Sol's cached-input price versus GPT-6 Sol and measured faster handling of long prompts, suggesting a possible architecture change, though not conclusive.
key_facts.excerpt: A new architecture for GPT-6.1 Sol? OpenAI halved its cached-input price compared with GPT-6 Sol. Our measurements show it also handles long prompts faster.

stories.headline: AI labs pledge $2.4B in compute and tools to Genesis Mission as Trump pushes 'Super Intelligence' label

key_facts.fact: At the White House 'Science: A New Golden Age' summit on October 8, eleven industry partners committed $2.4 billion in tools and compute credits to the Genesis Mission Consortium supporting over 15 federal agencies.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump Administration announced $2.4B in SI for science tools and compute credits for the Genesis Mission Consortium from eleven industry partners, which will support over 15 Federal agencies

key_facts.fact: Commitments include Nvidia $1B, AMD $500M, OpenAI $200M, Anthropic and Google $150M each, AMP and Emerald AI $100M each, and AWS, Armada, Crusoe and Micron $50M each.
key_facts.excerpt: Industry partner commitments include NVIDIA ($1B), AMD ($500M), OpenAI ($200M), $150M each from Anthropic and Google, $100M each from AMP and Emerald AI, and $50M each from AWS, Armada, Crusoe, and Micron.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's $200 million is in token discounts and training programs for scientists; Anthropic's $150 million over three years provides Claude access to agencies including NASA, NIH and NSF.
key_facts.excerpt: $200 million from OpenAI in token discounts and training programs for scientists, $150 million over three years in access to Anthropic's Claude

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said its funding will provide Claude, Claude Code and API credits to several hundred Genesis Mission research projects, with priorities including fusion energy and quantum computing.
key_facts.excerpt: Provide Claude, Claude Code, and API credits to several hundred Genesis Mission research projects; Partner closely with agencies and national laboratories on the administration's top science priorities, including fusion energy and quantum computing

key_facts.fact: The same day, Trump posted on Truth Social that the White House considers anyone using the term 'Artificial Intelligence' instead of 'Super Intelligence' to be 'THE ENEMY'.
key_facts.excerpt: Anyone who refuses to use the term "super intelligence," President Donald Trump's new preferred moniker for AI, is an "enemy" of the White House, Trump said in a Thursday afternoon social media post

key_facts.fact: The post escalates a September 29 executive order directing federal agencies to replace 'AI' with 'Super Intelligence' or 'SI' in official communications; the order keeps the existing statutory definition of AI.
key_facts.excerpt: the terms "Super Intelligence" and "SI" mean the technologies and systems encompassed by the term "artificial intelligence" as defined in section 9401(3) of title 15, United States Code.
